facets.label: Hume: proportion belief to evidence
facets.bach_take: Bach calls it 'the first rule of epistemology' and uses it to separate 'true/false' thinkers (nerds) from people who adopt beliefs for group membership.

mentions.quote: the first rule of epistemology says that the confidence in the belief must equal the weight of the evidence supporting it.
mentions.source: The Ghost in the Machine (35C3)

mentions.quote: everything that is not impossible is possible and the confidence gets assigned according to the evidence
mentions.source: The Operation of Consciousness (AGI-25, Reykjavik)

facets.bach_take: Bach says idealism and materialism are complementary: we do live in a dream, but the dreamer is a physical brain. Asked in 2024 about books claiming the universe emerges from consciousness, he replies that this explains nothing about how it works.

mentions.quote: So an alternative is idealism which says that there is only a mental world.
mentions.source: The Ghost in the Machine (35C3)

mentions.quote: So these ideas of materialism and idealism are not in opposition.
mentions.source: The Ghost in the Machine (35C3)

mentions.quote: we obviously do live in a dream
mentions.source: Joscha Bach Λ John Vervaeke: Mind, Idealism, Computation (Theories of Everything)

mentions.quote: the idealists have to explain why this dream looks in many parts so damn regular
mentions.source: Joscha Bach Λ John Vervaeke: Mind, Idealism, Computation (Theories of Everything)

mentions.quote: if Consciousness is fundamental I don’t know how it actually works
mentions.source: Self Models of Loving Grace (38C3)

facets.label: Leibniz
facets.bach_take: For Bach, Leibniz is where the project of mechanising thought begins in earnest: translating thoughts into numbers and resolving arguments by computation.

mentions.quote: Paraphrase (name garbled as 'li Nets'): Leibniz had the idea that we can translate thoughts and arguments into numbers and resolve arguments by calculation.
mentions.source: Synthetic Sentience (37C3)

mentions.quote: Paraphrase (garbled as 'lights'): Leibniz had the insight that you need to mathematize the mind and translate it into a kind of mathematical machine.
mentions.source: Cyber Animism (talk hosted by Michael Levin's center, Tufts)

facets.label: Leibniz's mill
facets.bach_take: Bach quotes the mill passage in 2018 and again in the 2025 CIMC essay. His answer is that Leibniz lacked the idea of a substrate-independent machine: perception belongs to the software-level model, not to the pushing parts.

mentions.quote: And what you are going to see is just parts pushing at each other.
mentions.source: How to Build a Mind: Artificial Intelligence Reloaded (30C3)

mentions.quote: Something that Leibniz describes, for instance, was a metaphor of a mill.
mentions.source: Joscha Bach: Time, Simulation Hypothesis, Existence (Theories of Everything with Curt Jaimungal)

mentions.quote: leibniz says this idea of imagine you could have a Mill and this this is your mind
mentions.source: Machine Learning Street Talk #82 – Dr. Joscha Bach: Digital Physics, DL and Consciousness [UNPLUGGED]

mentions.quote: that has been the dream of philosophers at least since leibniz
mentions.source: Joscha Bach and Connor Leahy [HQ VERSION] (Machine Learning Street Talk)

mentions.quote: What is a causal pattern? Right? We call it software.
mentions.source: Machine Learning Street Talk – Why Leibniz Couldn't Find the Mind Inside the Mill (Joscha Bach)

mentions.quote: Paraphrase (German): Leibniz imagined a machine that could produce thoughts, sensations and perception, enlarged so one could walk inside.
mentions.source: Machine Dreams (German-language lecture, Dresden / Datenspuren 2017)

mentions.quote: 'The absence of an understanding of substrate independent machines lead Leibniz to the rejection of mechanist philosophy', followed by the mill quotation (1714).
mentions.source: The Cortical Conductor Theory: Towards Addressing Consciousness in AI Models (BICA 2018)

mentions.quote: 'already three centuries ago, in his Monadology, Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz gives an illustration', followed by the mill quotation.
mentions.source: The Machine Consciousness Hypothesis (Joscha Bach & Hikari Sorensen, CIMC essay)

mentions.quote: Leibniz's New Essays (1704) is in the CIMC library.
mentions.source: cimc.ai library (reading list)

facets.bach_take: Bach and CIMC claim La Mettrie as an ancestor of the computational view of mind.

mentions.quote: we find it in La Mettrie, where he describes that, there must be systems of competing springs in the mind
mentions.source: The Jim Rutt Show EP72 – Joscha Bach on Minds, Machines & Magic

mentions.quote: Paraphrase (German): La Mettrie, a late contemporary of Leibniz, wrote 'L'homme machine' and held that the world is completely physical and man a kind of animal.
mentions.source: Machine Dreams (German-language lecture, Dresden / Datenspuren 2017)

mentions.quote: mentions 'Julien Offray de LaMettrie's (1748) remark that while minds are machines, these had to be thought of as “immortal” and “transcendental”'.
mentions.source: The Cortical Conductor Theory: Towards Addressing Consciousness in AI Models (BICA 2018)

mentions.quote: Paraphrase (garbled as 'Julian of f lri' and 'L machine'): La Mettrie had the insight that humans can be understood as machines and our motivation might be cybernetic, composed of opposing springs.
mentions.source: Synthetic Sentience (37C3)

mentions.quote: AI 'began with Aristotle and continued with people like Leibniz, La Mettrie, Frege, Tarski, and Wittgenstein'.
mentions.source: cimc.ai website (mission, research, grants text extracted from the JS bundle)

mentions.quote: L'Homme Machine (1748) is in the CIMC library.
mentions.source: cimc.ai library (reading list)

facets.bach_take: For Bach, rationalism and the Enlightenment were invented as an immunisation against 'mind viruses' such as religion.

mentions.quote: people have invented rationalism and enlightenment, basically to act as immunization against mind viruses.
mentions.source: Computational Meta-Psychology (32C3)

facets.label: Kant
facets.bach_take: Mentioned only in a Q&A answer: Bach doubts that morality can be defined outside a framework of social norms that people agree on.

mentions.quote: This project of defining morality without societies exists longer than Kant of course.
mentions.source: Computational Meta-Psychology (32C3)

facets.label: Critique of Pure Reason
facets.bach_take: CIMC has a stated project to connect the Critique to 20th-century computational philosophy, and its 'Prime Hypostasis' note starts from Kant. This is the work of Bach's colleagues Hildebrandt-Harangozó and Sorensen; no direct quotation of Bach on Kant was retrieved here.

mentions.quote: One current project is on connecting the Critique of Pure Reason to insights from computational philosophy from the twentieth century.
mentions.source: The California Institute for Machine Consciousness Research Program Whitepaper (Sorensen, Hildebrandt-Harangozó, de Kerhuelvez, Rutt, Bach)

mentions.quote: opens with Kant's closing section of the Prolegomena on putting metaphysics on a sound foundation.
mentions.source: Prime Hypostasis: A Short Reflection on the Idea that Provability + Hypostasis = Classical Semantics (Hildebrandt-Harangozó & Sorensen)

mentions.quote: Critique of Pure Reason (1781) is in the CIMC library.
mentions.source: cimc.ai library (reading list)

facets.bach_take: Bach calls it an unfinished attempt to recover ethics after Christianity, to 'repair morality in the rationalist age', and not a successful one.

mentions.quote: we should all serve the utility monster if it existed that's a problem with quantifying mental States
mentions.source: Synthetic Sentience (37C3)

mentions.quote: It was an unfinished attempt to recover ethics post Christianity.
mentions.source: Joscha Bach & Anders Sandberg - AI, Consciousness and the Cyborg Leviathan (Science, Technology & the Future)

mentions.quote: I think utilitarianism is an attempt to repair morality in the rationalist age, but I don't think it's a very successful one.
mentions.source: Joscha Bach PUSHES Roman Yampolskiy: Only ASI Can Save Us! (Dr Brian Keating)

facets.label: Romanticism
facets.bach_take: Bach names the literature of Romanticism and German poetry as a formative influence, and says he grew up in a region of Thuringia shaped by it.

mentions.quote: it's an area of German Romanticism which had a pretty big influence on how I grew up
mentions.source: Singularity.FM – Joscha Bach: We need to understand the nature of AI to understand who we are

mentions.quote: the classical philosophers and also the literature of romanticism
mentions.source: Lex Fridman Podcast #101 – Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality

mentions.quote: Paraphrase (garbled subtitles): as a result we got Romanticism, which is basically the fight against rationalism, to keep the sense of meaning and connection to something beyond.
mentions.source: Machine Dreams (33C3)

facets.label: Undine and The Little Mermaid
facets.bach_take: Bach tells both to his children instead of the Disney version, and uses them to say the mermaid is right: you sacrifice for romantic love. He also uses 'sirens eat people' as a parable about loving something that does not share your purposes.

mentions.quote: The Little Mermaid is a siren Sirens eat people
mentions.source: Singularity.FM – Joscha Bach: We need to understand the nature of AI to understand who we are

mentions.quote: And I think that the mermaid is right. You sacrifice your life for romantic love.
mentions.source: Lex Fridman Podcast #101 – Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality

facets.label: Fairy tales and Fairyland
facets.bach_take: Bach reads the motif 'one day in Fairyland is seven years in human land' as a possible folk memory of the idea that plant minds run on much slower time scales.

mentions.quote: It's very similar to what our ancestors claimed about the fairies, right?
mentions.source: AGI-24 keynote on cyber animism (Seattle; Machine Learning Street Talk recording)

mentions.quote: European fairy tales say that spirits of plants are sentient and populate the forest; one day in fairy land is seven years in human land.
mentions.source: Cyber Animism (talk hosted by Michael Levin's center, Tufts)

facets.bach_take: When an interviewer suggested AI is the universe's way of understanding itself, Bach called it a Hegelian thought: tempting and poetic, but not obviously informative.

mentions.quote: Another perspective on the LLM is that it's basically a weltgeist. That's a notion of Hegel.
mentions.source: AGI-24 keynote on cyber animism (Seattle; Machine Learning Street Talk recording)

mentions.quote: Well, it's a very Hegelian thought, right? And it's tempting and um it's very poetic.
mentions.source: This is the dawn of machine consciousness | Joscha Bach FULL INTERVIEW (Institute of Art and Ideas)

facets.bach_take: Bach's analogy for AI: asking 'what is intelligence?' in 1950 was like asking 'what is life?' before cell theory. He also calls the cell the smallest known universal machine for extracting negentropy.

mentions.quote: life oversells could not be discovered before 1839 when the cell theory came up.
mentions.source: Machine Dreams (33C3)

facets.bach_take: Bach relays a remark by the mathematician Misha Gromov that Darwin was the last person able to connect the dots in a completely fresh way; Bach himself thinks some philosophy is still being done, mostly in the foundations of mathematics.

mentions.quote: Misha gromov once told me he's a mathematician that in his perspective Darin was the last philosopher
mentions.source: Singularity.FM – Joscha Bach: We need to understand the nature of AI to understand who we are

facets.label: Marx
facets.bach_take: Bach grew up in East Germany and says he was a convinced Marxist at 16. He now cites that as a warning to his younger self about the unjustified certainty of activists.

mentions.quote: when I was 16 years old, I knew exactly what was in the best interest of the working class
mentions.source: Joscha Bach: Time, Simulation Hypothesis, Existence (Theories of Everything with Curt Jaimungal)

mentions.quote: I think that Marx was correct in saying that capitalism is prone to crisis.
mentions.source: Lex Fridman Podcast #212 – Joscha Bach: Nature of Reality, Dreams, and Consciousness

facets.label: Habermas and dialectical materialism
facets.bach_take: Bach's point is that after the Nazi era both Germanies lost their rigorous philosophical tradition.

mentions.quote: Western Germany didn't get much more edgy than Habermass
mentions.source: Lex Fridman Podcast #101 – Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality

facets.bach_take: Working notes record that Bach quotes a 19th-century statement of this kind in his German 2017 lecture, but the speaker's name is illegible in the ASR transcript.

mentions.quote: a 19th-century quotation on the limits of explaining consciousness; the name is unreadable in the German ASR text.
mentions.source: Machine Dreams (German-language lecture, Dresden / Datenspuren 2017)

butler.title: Samuel Butler and the Butlerian Jihad

facets.bach_take: Bach cites Butler as someone who saw the potential threat of superintelligence in great detail long before computers existed.

mentions.quote: Butler who after whom the Butlerian Jihad is named could see the potential threat to superintelligence much much earlier
mentions.source: The Panel Where Everyone Disagrees About Saving the World - Joscha Bach, David Pearce, Andrew Critch (California Institute for Machine Consciousness)

facets.bach_take: Bach's starting point for why infinities break mathematics: the contradictions show classical mathematics cannot be run without 'crashing'.

mentions.quote: Hilbert stumbled on counter set theoretic uh experiments to deal with natural numbers
mentions.source: Singularity.FM – Joscha Bach: We need to understand the nature of AI to understand who we are

mentions.quote: the cardinality of a set grows slower than the cardinality of the set of its subsets
mentions.source: The Ghost in the Machine (35C3)

mentions.quote: Hilbert saw that, for instance, a country's sets here where the experiments and mathematics led into contradictions.
mentions.source: Lex Fridman Podcast #101 – Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality

facets.bach_take: Bach rejects it twice: in 2014 as an inconvenient consequence of read-only dualism, and in 2025 with the quip that an epiphenomenalist's report is not caused by their consciousness, so you need not listen.

mentions.quote: this idea that consciousness has no causal role is called epiphenomenalism
mentions.source: The Operation of Consciousness (AGI-25, Reykjavik)

mentions.quote: Paraphrase (subtitle: 'This is called epiphenomenal, and it's a bit inconvenient'): if mind reads from but cannot write to the universe, experience is causally irrelevant.
mentions.source: From Computation to Consciousness (31C3)

facets.bach_take: Named as a post-Enlightenment thinker who did not yet have the 'hard problem', supporting Bach's claim that it is a 20th-century confusion.

mentions.quote: Paraphrase (captions: 'when you read Ga and uh Brenano'): they are post-Enlightenment and don't have this issue.
mentions.source: The Operation of Consciousness (AGI-25, Reykjavik)

facets.bach_take: Bach dislikes the word because it suggests a magical extra ingredient. He prefers to talk about causal patterns that are described at a coarser level.

mentions.quote: I don't like the word of emergence because it gives people an intuition that there is this magical thing
mentions.source: Joscha Bach - Why Your Thoughts Aren't Yours. (Machine Learning Street Talk)

facets.bach_take: Bach admires this era as psychology with real theories, before the field 'had an accident' and retreated into behaviourism and single-hypothesis experiments.

mentions.quote: Wilhelm Wundt and Fechner and Helmholtz did very beautiful experiments. Very nice psychology, very nice theories.
mentions.source: How to Build a Mind: Artificial Intelligence Reloaded (30C3)

facets.bach_take: Part of Bach's lineage of the AI project: Frege wanted a calculus for thinking.

mentions.quote: The people that are talking about reasoning professionally today Tarski and Frege and build on their work.
mentions.source: Lex Fridman Podcast #392 – Joscha Bach: Life, Intelligence, Consciousness, AI & the Future of Humans

mentions.quote: philosophers have understood this for a long time like since Dipenitz, Friger, Vitkinstein and so on
mentions.source: This is the dawn of machine consciousness | Joscha Bach FULL INTERVIEW (Institute of Art and Ideas)

mentions.quote: Paraphrase (garbled as 'godlo frer'): Gottlob Frege had the idea of coming up with a formal language for thinking.
mentions.source: Synthetic Sentience (37C3)

mentions.quote: Paraphrase (garbled as 'frager'): Frege built a calculus in which he hoped to be able to express thoughts.
mentions.source: Cyber Animism (talk hosted by Michael Levin's center, Tufts)

facets.bach_take: Bach reads Heidi as an embodiment of European Protestantism: a pure being committed to serving God whom civilisation exists to protect.

mentions.quote: Heidi is an embodiment of this spirit of European Protestantism
mentions.source: Lex Fridman Podcast #212 – Joscha Bach: Nature of Reality, Dreams, and Consciousness

facets.bach_take: Bach is irreverent: Nietzsche is smart and readable but took himself too seriously and ended in tragedy.

mentions.quote: I think that Nietzsche is the classical equivalent of a shit poster.
mentions.source: Lex Fridman Podcast #101 – Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality

facets.bach_take: Shown as a picture of looking behind the interface of experience at the mechanism that generates it.

mentions.quote: Paraphrase (captions: 'the famous flam Marian in raving of Unknown Origin first print in in 1888'): the Flammarion engraving describes the attempt to break out of the sphere of what you can perceive.
mentions.source: Self Models of Loving Grace (38C3)

facets.bach_take: Bach uses them to explain Gödel's method (arithmetic emulating logic) and notes that even 'zero' needs a number system, so non-existence is not a free default.

mentions.quote: He basically built an emulator using Peano arithmetic to express a logical language.
mentions.source: Machine Learning Street Talk – Why Leibniz Couldn't Find the Mind Inside the Mill (Joscha Bach)

mentions.quote: Bach: once you have Peano's axioms (captioned 'pianos axioms') you have a Turing-complete system from which a universe could be built.
mentions.source: Singularity.FM – Joscha Bach on AI, Cosmology, Existence and the Bible

mentions.quote: Paraphrase (garbled as 'pianos aums'): the computer Gödel found was Peano's axioms, which define the natural numbers and arithmetic over them.
mentions.source: Synthetic Sentience (37C3)

james.title: William James: The Principles of Psychology

facets.bach_take: Listed in the CIMC library. The CIMC essay names James, with Freud, Jung, Piaget and Leary, as someone who implicitly used the idea of a mind made of parts.

mentions.quote: the compositional psyche 'has been implicitly used by William James, Sigmund Freud, Carl Gustav Jung, Jean Piaget, Timothy Leary and many others'.
mentions.source: The Machine Consciousness Hypothesis (Joscha Bach & Hikari Sorensen, CIMC essay)

mentions.quote: Principles of Psychology (1890) is listed under classical texts.
mentions.source: cimc.ai library (reading list)

facets.bach_take: Bach says reading Wilde early 'inoculated' him with romanticism.

mentions.quote: I read Oscar Wilde before I read the other things
mentions.source: Lex Fridman Podcast #101 – Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality

facets.bach_take: Bach distinguishes it from his simulation speculations: a Boltzmann brain exists for one frame, whereas we remember a long sequence of states, which makes it very unlikely.

mentions.quote: Boltzmann brain is only there for one tick, for one frame, and then it falls apart again
mentions.source: Manifold #76 (Steve Hsu) – Joscha Bach: Consciousness and AGI

facets.bach_take: Bach speculates that cells could be the ideal von Neumann probe, compatible with panspermia, because he suspects spontaneous biogenesis is very unlikely. He says he is not asserting it.

mentions.quote: And I'm not suggesting that this is the case, but it would be compatible with the Prince Bermium hypothesis
mentions.source: Lex Fridman Podcast #101 – Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality

facets.bach_take: Central to Bach's worldview: constructive mathematics is 'the part of maths that works' and is the same thing as computation. Computationalism is a form of constructivism, and physics borrowed non-constructive mathematics before this was understood.

mentions.quote: Computation is constructive mathematics. The tiny, neglected subset of mathematics, where you have to show the money.
mentions.source: The Ghost in the Machine (35C3)

mentions.quote: constructive mathematics is the part of maths that works and it happens to be the same as computation
mentions.source: The Jim Rutt Show EP72 – Joscha Bach on Minds, Machines & Magic

mentions.quote: And constructive mathematics is roughly the same thing as computation.
mentions.source: The Jim Rutt Show EP87 – Joscha Bach on Theories of Consciousness

mentions.quote: constructive mathematics is the subset of mathematics that actually works
mentions.source: The Operation of Consciousness (AGI-25, Reykjavik)

mentions.quote: the claim of computationalism is separate. It's simply constructivism.
mentions.source: Salon with Stephen Wolfram × Joscha Bach_What if we had bigger brains. (California Institute for Machine Consciousness)

mentions.quote: something is real to the degree that is implemented
mentions.source: Salon with Stephen Wolfram × Joscha Bach_What if we had bigger brains. (California Institute for Machine Consciousness)

mentions.quote: I think in classical mathematics, the first formulation was Intuitionism.
mentions.source: Machine Learning Street Talk – Why Leibniz Couldn't Find the Mind Inside the Mill (Joscha Bach)

facets.label: Russell's paradox
facets.bach_take: A step in Bach's foundations story; he also mentions Russell's antinomy when answering a question about hierarchy in living systems.

mentions.quote: Does the set of the sets that doesn't contain themselves contain itself? If it does, it doesn't, and if it doesn't, it does.
mentions.source: The Ghost in the Machine (35C3)

facets.label: Principia Mathematica
facets.bach_take: Bach thinks the type restriction was too strong, since minds do build exactly the self-referential constructs it forbids, and that Gödel showed the attempt could not remove the contradictions anyway.

mentions.quote: And I think this was a limitation that was too strong because we think like this.
mentions.source: Why Consciousness Might Not Be Hard At All (Joscha Bach) (Machine Learning Street Talk)

mentions.quote: Russell and Whitehead and Principia Mathematica were attempting to do this by limiting set theory
mentions.source: Machine Learning Street Talk – Why Leibniz Couldn't Find the Mind Inside the Mill (Joscha Bach)

mentions.quote: Russell & Whitehead's Principia (1910-13) is cited in the section on the foundations of computation.
mentions.source: The Machine Consciousness Hypothesis (Joscha Bach & Hikari Sorensen, CIMC essay)

facets.bach_take: Bach uses Husserl to pose the problem, then offers a way out: a robot gets only bits at its interface, and a cognitive architecture can turn bits into something that looks like phenomena.

mentions.quote: Paraphrase (heavily garbled subtitles): reality is not given directly; we get phenomena, the mind turns them into noema, and the process is called noesis.
mentions.source: From Computation to Consciousness (31C3)

mentions.quote: Paraphrase (German): we could begin our journey with Edmund Husserl ... what we perceive of the world are appearances, phenomena; the process of turning them into ideas he calls noesis.
mentions.source: Machine Dreams (German-language lecture, Dresden / Datenspuren 2017)

facets.bach_take: For Bach this was the bug report that led Gödel and Turing to discover that only the computable part of mathematics works.

mentions.quote: So David Hilbert, who was some kind of a community manager back then, said: "Guys, fix this!
mentions.source: The Ghost in the Machine (35C3)

mentions.quote: which is in some sense what Grydol and Turing discovered in response to Hilbert's call
mentions.source: Lex Fridman Podcast #212 – Joscha Bach: Nature of Reality, Dreams, and Consciousness

mentions.quote: And so Gödel had this idea of trying to
mentions.source: Why Consciousness Might Not Be Hard At All (Joscha Bach) (Machine Learning Street Talk)

mentions.quote: All these issues led Hilbert to saying, please mathematicians, there seems to be something wrong here.
mentions.source: Machine Learning Street Talk – Why Leibniz Couldn't Find the Mind Inside the Mill (Joscha Bach)

facets.label: Wittgenstein
facets.bach_take: Bach says Wittgenstein pre-empted the logicist program of AI by decades and anticipated Turing's universality (logic from NAND gates). He sides with the late Wittgenstein: language is not fundamental to cognition, and images/perception were the unsolved part.

mentions.quote: Wittgenstein basically preempted the logitist program of AI that Minskie started 17:09 later
mentions.source: Lex Fridman Podcast #101 – Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality

mentions.quote: I agree with Wittgenstein. I just agree with the late Wittgenstein.
mentions.source: Lex Fridman Podcast #101 – Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality

mentions.quote: Turing was actually a pupil of Wittgenstein.
mentions.source: Lex Fridman Podcast #101 – Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality

mentions.quote: People have tried to mechanize the mind to turn it into a mathematical principle
mentions.source: This is the dawn of machine consciousness | Joscha Bach FULL INTERVIEW (Institute of Art and Ideas)

mentions.quote: who had this idea of turning English into some kind of general programming language
mentions.source: Joscha Bach & Anders Sandberg - AI, Consciousness and the Cyborg Leviathan (Science, Technology & the Future)

facets.label: Tractatus Logico-Philosophicus
facets.bach_take: Bach's thesis cites it for the habit of equating thought with language. The CIMC essay cites Russell's introduction to it for the point that all logic can be built from one operation (NAND); CIMC counts Wittgenstein among AI's philosophical ancestors.

mentions.quote: It's an attempt by a guy who was basically a coder, an AI scientist, to reverse engineer the language of his own thinking.
mentions.source: The Ghost in the Machine (35C3)

mentions.quote: I think that the track titles itself is probably the most beautiful philosophical text that was written in the 20th century.
mentions.source: Lex Fridman Podcast #101 – Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality

mentions.quote: 'since Wittgenstein (1921), thinking is generally quite often equated with linguistic productivity'.
mentions.source: Principles of Synthetic Intelligence: Building Blocks for an Architecture of Motivated Cognition (PhD dissertation draft, Universität Osnabrück)

mentions.quote: Wittgenstein had the idea of translating English into something like a programming language so philosophy could be true or false.
mentions.source: Synthetic Sentience (37C3)

mentions.quote: Bach: it was 'already known to Wittgenstein', as explained in Russell's introduction to the Tractatus, that 'you only need the ... not-and operator to build all the entire logic'
mentions.source: Joscha Bach: Consciousness, Artificial Intelligence, and the Threat of AI Apocalypse (Robinson Erhardt / Robinson's Podcast)

mentions.quote: 'As Bertrand Russell anticipates in the 1922 introduction to Wittgenstein's Tractatus', it is in principle sufficient to use combinations of Not-AND operations.
mentions.source: The Machine Consciousness Hypothesis (Joscha Bach & Hikari Sorensen, CIMC essay)

mentions.quote: 'The Missing Institute' text says AI began with Aristotle and continued with Leibniz, La Mettrie, Frege, Tarski and Wittgenstein.
mentions.source: cimc.ai website (mission, research, grants text extracted from the JS bundle)

mentions.quote: Tractatus (1921) is in the CIMC library under classical texts.
mentions.source: cimc.ai library (reading list)

facets.label: Philosophical Investigations
facets.bach_take: Bach presents it as Wittgenstein's admission that the Tractatus project failed because the world is too ambiguous, the same wall symbolic AI later hit.

mentions.quote: In the end he wrote the book "Philosophical Investigations", where he concluded, that his project basically failed.
mentions.source: The Ghost in the Machine (35C3)

mentions.quote: he looked at this in his book at the end of his life, philosophical investigations, was the notion of images
mentions.source: Lex Fridman Podcast #101 – Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality

facets.bach_take: In 2013 Bach calls psychoanalysis a hermeneutic, non-falsifiable enterprise that pushed psychology into behaviourism. A decade later he says Freud's architecture resembles his own: motivation and emotion (the 'it') projected into a personal self.

mentions.quote: And psycho analysis is not a natural science, but it’s a hermeneutic science. You cannot disprove it scientifically.
mentions.source: How to Build a Mind: Artificial Intelligence Reloaded (30C3)

mentions.quote: It's quite similar to how Freud sees the mind
mentions.source: AGI-24 keynote on cyber animism (Seattle; Machine Learning Street Talk recording)

mentions.quote: Paraphrase (garbled as 'sigon FR'): Sigmund Freud had a very similar idea of how the mind is organized: the 'it', the ego and the super ego.
mentions.source: Synthetic Sentience (37C3)

facets.bach_take: Quoted in his discussion of suffering and living in the present moment.

mentions.quote: one day I will die, all the other days I will not
mentions.source: The Operation of Consciousness (AGI-25, Reykjavik)

facets.label: Qualia
facets.bach_take: Bach treats qualia as feature dimensions of the brain's model, implementable as geometric representations. You can deconstruct them in meditation and notice that they are representations.

mentions.quote: Qualia are the features of experience.
mentions.source: Joscha Bach: Time, Simulation Hypothesis, Existence (Theories of Everything with Curt Jaimungal)

mentions.quote: philosophers have introduced the term qualia to talk about perceptual features
mentions.source: Self Models of Loving Grace (38C3)

mentions.quote: you can deconstruct your qualia you can notice that they're just representing
mentions.source: Why consciousness is software, and software is spirit | Joscha Bach | FULL INTERVIEW (Institute of Art and Ideas)

facets.label: Mary's room (Epiphenomenal Qualia)
facets.bach_take: It is the first entry in the reference list of Bach's 2008 paper, as one of the philosophical objections that AI has to face. No detailed reply to it was found in the retrieved text.

mentions.quote: reference [1] Jackson, F. (1982). Epiphenomenal qualia. Philosophical Quarterly 32.
mentions.source: Seven Principles of Synthetic Intelligence (Proc. 1st Conference on Artificial General Intelligence, Memphis, pp. 63-74)

facets.bach_take: Bach's distinctive reading: Gödel did not find a limit of computation but a bug in classical, stateless mathematics with infinities. The fix is to use only constructive (computable) mathematics. He stresses that Gödel himself, a Platonist, was shocked by the result.

mentions.quote: as soon as we allow these kinds of loops - and we cannot really exclude these loops - then our mathematics crashes.
mentions.source: The Ghost in the Machine (35C3)

mentions.quote: It basically 16:02 shook his world to the core
mentions.source: Lex Fridman Podcast #101 – Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality

mentions.quote: And what Gödel has shown in my view is that constructive mathematics is real
mentions.source: The Jim Rutt Show EP87 – Joscha Bach on Theories of Consciousness

mentions.quote: classical mathematics that contains infinities cannot be implemented, cannot be real
mentions.source: The Jim Rutt Show EP87: Joscha Bach on Theories of Consciousness (transcript)

mentions.quote: girdle was a true realist that is he thought that truth really exists out there
mentions.source: Machine Learning Street Talk #82 – Dr. Joscha Bach: Digital Physics, DL and Consciousness [UNPLUGGED]

mentions.quote: There is no deeper notion of truth than proof.
mentions.source: Donald Hoffman Λ Joscha Bach: Consciousness, Gödel, Reality (Theories of Everything)

mentions.quote: A way to interpret Gödel's proof is that languages that cannot be automatically evaluated inevitably contain unresolvable paradoxes
mentions.source: The Machine Consciousness Hypothesis (Joscha Bach & Hikari Sorensen, CIMC essay)

mentions.quote: He basically built an emulator using Peano arithmetic
mentions.source: Why Consciousness Might Not Be Hard At All (Joscha Bach) (Machine Learning Street Talk)

mentions.quote: And what Gödel has discovered is that these bugs cannot be eliminated except by redefining the programming language of mathematics.
mentions.source: Machine Learning Street Talk – Why Leibniz Couldn't Find the Mind Inside the Mill (Joscha Bach)

mentions.quote: some philosophers argue humans can always decide what formal systems cannot, so they are more powerful than computers; 'Gödel has done this' proof for formal systems.
mentions.source: How to Build a Mind: Artificial Intelligence Reloaded (30C3)

mentions.quote: Paraphrase (name garbled as 'C girdle'/'could G'): Gödel 'invented the emulator' by defining a logical language on top of Peano's axioms, and found that stateless mathematics leads to contradictions.
mentions.source: Synthetic Sentience (37C3)

mentions.quote: some philosophers take Gödel to mean there are proofs only humans can make; Bach notes no AI company employs people to keep such proofs out of the computer.
mentions.source: The Operation of Consciousness (AGI-25, Reykjavik)

facets.bach_take: A brief stop in Bach's lineage: Tarski 'formalized logic for us' and fixed problems Aristotle did not see.

mentions.quote: taski formalized Logic for us
mentions.source: Synthetic Sentience (37C3)

mentions.quote: tarski who made progress and fixing the issues with logic that Aristotle didn't see yet
mentions.source: Cyber Animism (talk hosted by Michael Levin's center, Tufts)

facets.label: Alan Turing
facets.bach_take: Bach reads the Turing test as Turing asking whether he himself can understand intelligence. He notes Turing worried about telepathy, and credits Turing's reaction-diffusion work as the origin of a neglected self-organising branch of computing.

mentions.quote: I think that Turing could see that the solution is to understand that the question mathematics was computation all along
mentions.source: Lex Fridman Podcast #101 – Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality

mentions.quote: as long as brains are Turing complete, you can build minds on different substrates
mentions.source: The Jim Rutt Show EP87 – Joscha Bach on Theories of Consciousness

mentions.quote: is there's a possibility that telepathy is true
mentions.source: Donald Hoffman Λ Joscha Bach: Consciousness, Gödel, Reality (Theories of Everything)

mentions.quote: And so for me Turing's test is not so much a test for a machine.
mentions.source: Joscha Bach: "You Are Not Who You Think You Are!" (Dr Brian Keating, Into the Impossible)

facets.label: Church–Turing thesis
facets.bach_take: A cornerstone of every Bach lecture: because all computational languages have the same power, it does not matter which one describes mind or universe.

mentions.quote: all the computational approaches have the same power, although all the other ones that you are able to find in the future too, is called the Church-Turing thesis.
mentions.source: How to Build a Mind: Artificial Intelligence Reloaded (30C3)

mentions.quote: So, in some sense IIT is not compatible with the Church-Turing thesis
mentions.source: The Jim Rutt Show Currents 083 – Joscha Bach on Synthetic Intelligence

mentions.quote: It's the insight that every computer can emulate every other computer.
mentions.source: Why Consciousness Might Not Be Hard At All (Joscha Bach) (Machine Learning Street Talk)

mentions.quote: It's the insight that every computer can emulate every other computer.
mentions.source: Machine Learning Street Talk – Why Leibniz Couldn't Find the Mind Inside the Mill (Joscha Bach)

mentions.quote: Church and Turing discovered that all implementable representational languages have the same power.
mentions.source: Synthetic Sentience (37C3)

mentions.quote: Bach notes it 'is a thesis, it's not proved, so it's a conjecture'
mentions.source: Joscha Bach: Consciousness, Artificial Intelligence, and the Threat of AI Apocalypse (Robinson Erhardt / Robinson's Podcast)

mentions.quote: Python, assembler, the Turing machine or the lambda calculus can all be compiled into each other; 'that's called the Church-Turing thesis'.
mentions.source: The Operation of Consciousness (AGI-25, Reykjavik)

facets.label: The Turing machine
facets.bach_take: Bach calls it a good definition but a bad metaphor, because it leaves people imagining cogs and tape. He uses it to argue that minds are computational and in fact less than Turing machines, since real systems are finite.

mentions.quote: The Turing machine is a good definition, but it's a very bad metaphor
mentions.source: How to Build a Mind: Artificial Intelligence Reloaded (30C3)

mentions.quote: It's actually much more troubling: minds are fundamentally less than Turing machines!
mentions.source: How to Build a Mind: Artificial Intelligence Reloaded (30C3)

mentions.quote: defines a universe-computing machine with a state vector of bits, a position and instructions, 'With this, we can define the Turing machine'.
mentions.source: From Computation to Consciousness (31C3)

facets.label: Halting problem
facets.bach_take: Bach lists it among the true limits of computers and argues humans cannot solve such problems either.

mentions.quote: For instance the question whether a Turing machine ever stops for an arbitrary program.
mentions.source: How to Build a Mind: Artificial Intelligence Reloaded (30C3)

mentions.quote: then we cannot know whether this proof terminates.
mentions.source: The Ghost in the Machine (35C3)

facets.label: Post machine
facets.bach_take: Named in passing as one of many equivalent definitions of computation.

mentions.quote: For instance the post machine, which is a variation of the Turing machine
mentions.source: How to Build a Mind: Artificial Intelligence Reloaded (30C3)

facets.label: Computing Machinery and Intelligence (the Turing test)
facets.bach_take: Bach notes that Turing took telepathy seriously, and that the Turing test is about performance and so cannot test for consciousness. A true test would be an AI that explains how AI works.

mentions.quote: When Alan Turing wrote his paper “Computing Machinery and Intelligence” and those of you who haven’t read it should do so.
mentions.source: How to Build a Mind: Artificial Intelligence Reloaded (30C3)

mentions.quote: Turing’s famous 1950 paper in which he describes the Turing test, he does speculate about telepathy
mentions.source: Lex Fridman Podcast #392 – Joscha Bach: Life, Intelligence, Consciousness, AI & the Future of Humans

mentions.quote: in the 1950 paper that Alan Turing talks about the Turing test. He also discusses the possibility of telepathy
mentions.source: The Operation of Consciousness (AGI-25, Reykjavik)

mentions.quote: I think that a true Turing test would require that an AGI explains how AGI works.
mentions.source: Manifold #76 (Steve Hsu) – Joscha Bach: Consciousness and AGI

mentions.quote: Consciousness is by its nature not an externally visible performance, but a particular way to achieve a performance
mentions.source: The Machine Consciousness Hypothesis (Joscha Bach & Hikari Sorensen, CIMC essay)

mentions.quote: Turing's test does not care about how you produce the dialogue
mentions.source: Machine Learning Street Talk – Why Leibniz Couldn't Find the Mind Inside the Mill (Joscha Bach)

facets.label: Lambda calculus
facets.bach_take: This equivalence is the base of Bach's computationalism: any system that can be described precisely can be implemented on any universal computer. He calls computation the 20th century's most important idea.

mentions.quote: It's computation without wheels. It was invented basically at the same time as the Turing machine.
mentions.source: How to Build a Mind: Artificial Intelligence Reloaded (30C3)

mentions.quote: Computationalism is the new mechanism
mentions.source: Everything Is Computation (Edge Question 2016)

mentions.quote: he figured out together with Alonzo Church - not together, independently but at the same time
mentions.source: The Ghost in the Machine (35C3)

mentions.quote: the Lambda calculus and the turing machine turn out to have the same power
mentions.source: Machine Learning Street Talk #82 – Dr. Joscha Bach: Digital Physics, DL and Consciousness [UNPLUGGED]

mentions.quote: The Turing machine is a very special case of a rewrite system.
mentions.source: The Jim Rutt Show Currents 083 – Joscha Bach on Synthetic Intelligence

mentions.quote: an unbounded state-transition system 'becomes a Turing Machine, or a Lambda Calculus, or a Post machine, or one of the many other, mutually equivalent formalisms'.
mentions.source: Everything Is Computation (Edge Question 2016)

mentions.quote: cites Church 1936, Schönfinkel 1924 and the Turing machine as equivalent models of computation.
mentions.source: The Machine Consciousness Hypothesis (Joscha Bach & Hikari Sorensen, CIMC essay)

facets.label: Moses Schönfinkel
facets.bach_take: Named among those who defined languages built from automata that make computation practical.

mentions.quote: Paraphrase (garbled as 'Moses shink'): Moses Schönfinkel and many others defined languages that allow computation to run efficiently in practice.
mentions.source: Synthetic Sentience (37C3)

facets.bach_take: Bach's standing complaint about psychology. He says radical behaviourism is easy to refute (purely reactive systems are harder to build than representational ones) and that a 'pragmatic behaviourism' still keeps psychologists from theorising.

mentions.quote: People like Skinner believe that there is no such thing as mental representations.
mentions.source: How to Build a Mind: Artificial Intelligence Reloaded (30C3)

mentions.quote: he was not himself denying the reality of mental states
mentions.source: The Jim Rutt Show EP 334 – Worldviews: Joscha Bach

mentions.quote: his psychology professor claimed dogs have no mental states, only stimulus-reaction patterns; Bach replies that a lookup table would be far harder than mental states.
mentions.source: Self Models of Loving Grace (38C3)

maslow.title: Maslow: A Theory of Human Motivation

facets.bach_take: Cited in Bach's 2018 attention-learning paper next to his own MicroPsi model of motivation. How far he follows Maslow was not checked in the text.

mentions.quote: reference 7. Maslow, A.H. A theory of human motivation. Psychological Review 50 (4) 1943.
mentions.source: Attention Based Learning as a Foundation for Conscious Agents (position paper, Harvard PED affiliation)

facets.bach_take: A step in Bach's history of AI between symbol systems and autonomous agents.

mentions.quote: With McClelland and Pitts and so on. Parallel distributed processing.
mentions.source: How to Build a Mind: Artificial Intelligence Reloaded (30C3)

facets.bach_take: Bach defines government game-theoretically, as an agent that shifts payoffs so that selfish equilibria line up with the common good, and says the Catholic Church implemented game-theoretic principles.

mentions.quote: an agent that imposes an offset on your payout metrics to make your Nash equilibrium compatible with the common good
mentions.source: Lex Fridman Podcast #101 – Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality

facets.bach_take: A constant theme: 'Entropy is the enemy'. Bach defines cells and life as systems that harvest negentropy, and ties it to reversible computing: deleting bits requires a place to dump them.

mentions.quote: That's why we need to push back entropy. Entropy is the enemy.
mentions.source: From Computation to Consciousness (31C3)

mentions.quote: Paraphrase (subtitle 'Nick entropy'): a cell is the smallest universal machine we know that can extract negentropy over a wide range of environments.
mentions.source: Machine Dreams (33C3)

vonneumann.title: John von Neumann and the first computers

facets.label: John von Neumann
facets.bach_take: Bach calls the cell a possible von Neumann probe, and uses 'von Neumann computer' when describing Tononi's claim that ordinary computers cannot be conscious.

mentions.quote: So in a way, it's tempting to think of the cell as a von Neumann probe.
mentions.source: Lex Fridman Podcast #101 – Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality

mentions.quote: But a von Neumann computer can never be conscious.
mentions.source: Manifold #76 (Steve Hsu) – Joscha Bach: Consciousness and AGI

mentions.quote: there were people like John von Neumann who could see this much much earlier
mentions.source: The Panel Where Everyone Disagrees About Saving the World - Joscha Bach, David Pearce, Andrew Critch (California Institute for Machine Consciousness)

facets.label: Babbage, Zuse, von Neumann
facets.bach_take: Named as the people who turned the abstract idea of computability into machines.

mentions.quote: And came towards Babage and Zuse and von Neumann and so on.
mentions.source: How to Build a Mind: Artificial Intelligence Reloaded (30C3)

mentions.quote: Paraphrase (garbled as 'conver zuza and John for noyman'): Konrad Zuse and John von Neumann defined physically realizable automata.
mentions.source: Synthetic Sentience (37C3)

facets.label: Reliable organisms from unreliable components
facets.bach_take: Bach and Sorensen cite it to say that a computer does not need a deterministic substrate, which matters for brains made of noisy cells.

mentions.quote: 'as John von Neumann and others note, determinism can be achieved on indeterministic (noisy, probabilistic) substrates'.
mentions.source: The Machine Consciousness Hypothesis (Joscha Bach & Hikari Sorensen, CIMC essay)

facets.label: Information theory
facets.bach_take: Bach's metaphysics starts from it: all the universe gives us is information, 'discernible differences'. As a programmer he cares less about channel capacity than about what model the information encodes.

mentions.quote: Then we had information theory by Claude Shannon.
mentions.source: How to Build a Mind: Artificial Intelligence Reloaded (30C3)

mentions.quote: it's not so much important to look at Shannon information. I look at what we need to describe the evolution of a system.
mentions.source: The Ghost in the Machine (35C3)

facets.label: Computer chess
facets.bach_take: Bach uses the two strategies (careful long plan versus brute force) as an analogy for human thinking versus LLMs brute-forcing thought.

mentions.quote: Claude Shannon had this… When you describe chess suggested that there are two main strategies in which you could play chess.
mentions.source: Lex Fridman Podcast #392 – Joscha Bach: Life, Intelligence, Consciousness, AI & the Future of Humans

facets.label: Cybernetics
facets.bach_take: A foundation of Bach's thinking. He defines an agent as a controller with a set-point generator, sees motivation as nested feedback loops, and regrets that Minsky helped end cybernetics as a field in the US.

mentions.quote: Unfortunately hass been killed by second-order Cybernetics. By this Maturana stuff and so on.
mentions.source: How to Build a Mind: Artificial Intelligence Reloaded (30C3)

mentions.quote: The notion of a controller comes from cybernetics and control theory.
mentions.source: Lex Fridman Podcast #212 – Joscha Bach: Nature of Reality, Dreams, and Consciousness

mentions.quote: they're basically cybernetic feedback loops
mentions.source: Lex Fridman Podcast #212 – Joscha Bach: Nature of Reality, Dreams, and Consciousness

mentions.quote: we can understand motivation from the perspective of control theory and cybernetics
mentions.source: Joscha Bach: Consciousness, Artificial Intelligence, and the Threat of AI Apocalypse (Robinson Erhardt / Robinson's Podcast)

mentions.quote: I came to understand them as a cybernetic construct
mentions.source: Machine Consciousness & AI Awakening - Davidad and Joscha Bach (California Institute for Machine Consciousness)

mentions.quote: 'The description of such systems is the domain of cybernetics or systems science (Wiener 1948, Ashby 1956, von Bertalanffy 1968, Bischof 1968, Bateson 1972, Klir 1992).'
mentions.source: Principles of Synthetic Intelligence: Building Blocks for an Architecture of Motivated Cognition (PhD dissertation draft, Universität Osnabrück)

mentions.quote: Bach, J. (2010): Kybernetik. In Sandkühler (ed.), Enzyklopädie Philosophie, Felix-Meiner-Verlag.
mentions.source: Joscha Bach, Curriculum Vitae, July 14, 2023

facets.label: Project Cybersyn
facets.bach_take: Bach's example of an attempt to give society a centralised reward system like the brain's dopamine. 'Maybe it would have worked, who knows?'

mentions.quote: So Allende invited a bunch of cyberneticians to redesign the Chilean economy.
mentions.source: Computational Meta-Psychology (32C3)

facets.bach_take: Bach says the West's ethics used to rest on 'divine will', meaning what the best possible collective agent would want, acted out through us. He says this was lost, survives in the German constitution, and that utilitarianism is a weak replacement.

mentions.quote: it's still in the German Constitution but it's something that a lot of people don't really understand anymore
mentions.source: Synthetic Sentience (37C3)

facets.label: Physicalism
facets.bach_take: Bach defines it by two claims: there is a causally closed mechanical layer, and we supervene on it directly rather than living in someone's simulation. He accepts it, while insisting that information, not matter, is what we actually observe.

mentions.quote: matter is primary and mind emerges over functionality of matter, which is I think the dominant theory today and usually, we call it physicalism.
mentions.source: How to Build a Mind: Artificial Intelligence Reloaded (30C3)

mentions.quote: not because I think that physicalism is wrong
mentions.source: Conversation between Joscha Bach, Chris Fields, and Michael Levin (Michael Levin's Academic Content)

mentions.quote: And so physicalism is these two
mentions.source: Why Consciousness Might Not Be Hard At All (Joscha Bach) (Machine Learning Street Talk)

facets.label: Direct realism
facets.bach_take: Listed as one point in the space of possible metaphysics. Bach rejects it: what we experience is a model generated by the brain.

mentions.quote: reality is roughly as we experience it which is called direct realism
mentions.source: The Operation of Consciousness (AGI-25, Reykjavik)

facets.bach_take: Bach sees this small tradition as better suited to understanding minds than mainstream deep learning, because brains are built 'inside out' by self-organising units.

mentions.quote: there is something that is a very close analog that is a neural cellular automaton
mentions.source: Michael Levin Λ Joscha Bach: Collective Intelligence (Theories of Everything)

mentions.quote: when he looked at reaction diffusion patterns as a way to implement computation
mentions.source: Joscha Bach Λ Ben Goertzel: Conscious Ai, LLMs, AGI (Theories of Everything)

mentions.quote: the tradition of self-organization 'has been started by Turing in the 1950s' but was never followed up much.
mentions.source: Synthetic Sentience (37C3)

mentions.quote: this thread of AI started with Turing's work on reaction-diffusion models that he tried to get to compute.
mentions.source: Cyber Animism (talk hosted by Michael Levin's center, Tufts)

facets.bach_take: Bach is not ready to dismiss such reports. If telepathy were real, he thinks it would not overturn physics but would change neuroscience toward a view of brains as coupled resonators.

mentions.quote: The MKUltra program, and related programs were looking also into clairvoyance
mentions.source: The Jim Rutt Show EP87 – Joscha Bach on Theories of Consciousness

mentions.quote: Lex reads Bach's tweet: establishing telepathy would not force an update of physics but could trigger a revolution in neuroscience and AI.
mentions.source: Lex Fridman Podcast #392 – Joscha Bach: Life, Intelligence, Consciousness, AI & the Future of Humans

facets.bach_take: Bach names them as earlier stage models before giving his own seven 'Levels of Lucidity'. His thesis cites Piaget as a rare case of a unified theory in psychology.

mentions.quote: 'Piaget's work (especially Piaget 1954) might be one of the notable exceptions' to psychology's preference for small microtheories.
mentions.source: Principles of Synthetic Intelligence: Building Blocks for an Architecture of Motivated Cognition (PhD dissertation draft, Universität Osnabrück)

mentions.quote: mentions 'Piaget's famous four-stage model of childhood development, Jane Loevinger's nine stages of ego development, Lawrence Kohlberg's six stages of moral development'.
mentions.source: Levels of Lucidity (Joscha Bach, Substack)

facets.bach_take: Listed in the CIMC library under classical texts. No comment by Bach was retrieved.

mentions.quote: Doors of Perception (1954) is listed under classical texts.
mentions.source: cimc.ai library (reading list)

facets.bach_take: Curt asked whether Frodo feels anything, since Bach says we are characters in a story the brain tells itself. Bach replied that it depends on what is taken as the reality; the difference is that the brain's story is computed in real time and coupled to a body.

mentions.quote: we are characters in a story that the brain is telling itself
mentions.source: Joscha Bach: Time, Simulation Hypothesis, Existence (Theories of Everything with Curt Jaimungal)

facets.label: The Dartmouth workshop
facets.bach_take: Bach stresses that the founders wanted what is now called AGI, as a way to understand the mind, and that the field later retreated to narrow, fundable applications.

mentions.quote: which got together in the Dartmouth conference. It was in 1956.
mentions.source: How to Build a Mind: Artificial Intelligence Reloaded (30C3)

mentions.quote: they basically thought this is going to be an extended summer project
mentions.source: The Jim Rutt Show EP72 – Joscha Bach on Minds, Machines & Magic

mentions.quote: Because Minsky and McCarthy and others of course wanted to build AGI from the start
mentions.source: The Jim Rutt Show Currents 083 – Joscha Bach on Synthetic Intelligence

facets.label: John McCarthy
facets.bach_take: Named by Bach with Minsky as a founder of AI, understood as the recognition that computers offer a new paradigm for studying mind.

mentions.quote: the guy who came up with Lisp, McCarthy, he didn’t think that it would be a proper language.
mentions.source: How to Build a Mind: Artificial Intelligence Reloaded (30C3)

mentions.quote: it is a field that was started by Marvin Minsky and John McCarthy and a few others
mentions.source: Joscha Bach: Consciousness, Artificial Intelligence, and the Threat of AI Apocalypse (Robinson Erhardt / Robinson's Podcast)

mentions.quote: cites (McCarthy 1979) for a self-representation that is intensional and not only extensional.
mentions.source: Principles of Synthetic Intelligence: Building Blocks for an Architecture of Motivated Cognition (PhD dissertation draft, Universität Osnabrück)

facets.bach_take: Central to Bach's model: columns are nature's way of giving noisy neurons a standard interface, 'like lego bricks'. He imagines them as small state machines that link up, trade reward and approximate Solomonoff induction.

mentions.quote: And I think that nature solution to this is cortical columns. Cortical column is a circuit of between 100 and 400 neurons.
mentions.source: Computational Meta-Psychology (32C3)

mentions.quote: cortical columns, about 100 million of them, are probably something like a state machine that takes care of neural binding.
mentions.source: Machine Dreams (33C3)

mentions.quote: his proposed implementation is derived from an idea of how cortical columns work, on top of a state machine that sends control messages.
mentions.source: The Operation of Consciousness (AGI-25, Reykjavik)

facets.bach_take: Bach distinguishes it from his own picture: it is a mathematical paradigm in which parts of the universe's description stop causally influencing each other.

mentions.quote: the universe splits into copies of itself is a slightly different conception
mentions.source: Joscha Bach: Time, Simulation Hypothesis, Existence (Theories of Everything with Curt Jaimungal)

facets.label: Marvin Minsky
facets.bach_take: Bach calls him the most influential recent thinker on the nature of minds and opens his conductor paper with a Minsky epigraph. He borrows Minsky's remark that 'consciousness' is a suitcase word.

mentions.quote: It's a suitcase term that stands for a bunch of very different mechanisms.
mentions.source: From Computation to Consciousness (31C3)

mentions.quote: Marvin Minsky was quite certainly the most influential thinker about the nature of our minds in recent history.
mentions.source: On Marvin Minsky (bach.ai blog)

mentions.quote: So Marvin Minsky said, no, we cannot leave us with these guys because they don't know what they're doing anymore, minds are information processing systems.
mentions.source: Machine Dreams (33C3)

mentions.quote: This has lead Marvin Minsky (2006) to call consciousness “a suitcase term”, a notion that is notoriously hard to unpack.
mentions.source: The Cortical Conductor Theory: Towards Addressing Consciousness in AI Models (BICA 2018)

mentions.quote: When Minsky claimed that cognitive AI was in some sense, the same thing as symbolic AI, I think he made the wrong bet.
mentions.source: The Jim Rutt Show EP72 – Joscha Bach on Minds, Machines & Magic

mentions.quote: minsky was a part of a different era he was part of the modernist era of ai
mentions.source: Singularity.FM – Joscha Bach on AI, Cosmology, Existence and the Bible

mentions.quote: I had the honor of visiting him quite a few times in the last year of his life
mentions.source: Joscha Bach and Connor Leahy [HQ VERSION] (Machine Learning Street Talk)

mentions.quote: they antagonized each other and I think this delayed the progress of the field
mentions.source: The Spirit in the Machine | feat. Joscha Bach (AM I? podcast; YouTube also shows the alternate titles 'The Quest to Build Conscious AI' and 'Deepfaking the Human Mind')

mentions.quote: listed in the dissertation bibliography with Minsky (1975) on frames, The Society of Mind (1986) and The Emotion Machine (2006).
mentions.source: Principles of Synthetic Intelligence: Building Blocks for an Architecture of Motivated Cognition (PhD dissertation draft, Universität Osnabrück)

mentions.quote: at Dartmouth 'Marvin Minsky coined the name artificial intelligence'.
mentions.source: How to Build a Mind: Artificial Intelligence Reloaded (30C3)

mentions.quote: The Society of Mind (1985 in the list) appears under modern texts in the CIMC library.
mentions.source: cimc.ai library (reading list)

facets.label: The Society of Mind
facets.bach_take: Bach thinks future transformer-like systems will rediscover K-lines as an integrated attention hierarchy, and uses 'society of mind' when asking how autonomous agents can cooperate.

mentions.quote: future developments of the transformer algorithms are going to rediscover minsky's ideas of the k lines
mentions.source: Singularity.FM – Joscha Bach on AI, Cosmology, Existence and the Bible

mentions.quote: how can you make a society of mind out of multiple agents that are autonomous?
mentions.source: The Jim Rutt Show Currents 083 – Joscha Bach on Synthetic Intelligence

mentions.quote: he saw the mind as an interaction of agents that have a degree of autonomy and that at the same time have to achieve coherence
mentions.source: Joscha Bach and Connor Leahy [HQ VERSION] (Machine Learning Street Talk)

facets.label: Perceptrons
facets.bach_take: Bach's example of a wrong argument that cut off funding for a whole approach; people later found a way around it.

mentions.quote: In 1969 Minsky and Papert wrote a small booklet against the idea of using your neural networks.
mentions.source: How to Build a Mind: Artificial Intelligence Reloaded (30C3)

mentions.quote: Marvin Minsky wrote a book where he thought he had proven that the neural networks cannot converge over multiple layers
mentions.source: Machine Learning Street Talk #82 – Dr. Joscha Bach: Digital Physics, DL and Consciousness [UNPLUGGED]

facets.bach_take: Bach deeply respects him as one of the great minds of his generation, but calls him a 'mysterian' who has not followed AI developments and should update on what generative models now do.

mentions.quote: Chomsky is probably one of the greatest minds of his generation
mentions.source: The Jim Rutt Show EP87 – Joscha Bach on Theories of Consciousness

mentions.quote: Noam Chomsky is a mysterious with respect to the mind.
mentions.source: Donald Hoffman Λ Joscha Bach: Consciousness, Gödel, Reality (Theories of Everything)

mentions.quote: i think it would be amazing if chomsky would update on this
mentions.source: Singularity.FM – Joscha Bach on AI, Cosmology, Existence and the Bible

mentions.quote: Paraphrase (captions: 'chsky was creating Linguistics'): next door somebody like Minsky was creating AI and Chomsky was creating linguistics.
mentions.source: Cyber Animism (talk hosted by Michael Levin's center, Tufts)

facets.bach_take: Bach points out that Dennett's pandemonium picture of mind goes back to Selfridge, Minsky's teacher, and explains it as behaviours on a stage evaluated by an audience of other behaviours.

mentions.quote: The pandemonium theory by the way goes back to Selfridge
mentions.source: The Jim Rutt Show EP87 – Joscha Bach on Theories of Consciousness

facets.label: Functionalism
facets.bach_take: Bach's stated position from 2018 onward. By 2025 he calls it 'computationalist functionalism' and insists it is a metaphysical stance about how we construct objects from observed behaviour, not an empirical claim that laptops can think.

mentions.quote: And the answer that I am suggesting, is functionalism which means that indeed we exist only in a dream.
mentions.source: The Ghost in the Machine (35C3)

mentions.quote: functionalism is the rejection of the notion of a hidden essence
mentions.source: The Jim Rutt Show EP87 – Joscha Bach on Theories of Consciousness

mentions.quote: one of the foundations of this thinking is computationalist functionalism
mentions.source: "We Are All Software" - Joscha Bach (Machine Learning Street Talk)

mentions.quote: Computationalism is a theory of representation and functionalism is a theory of epistemology.
mentions.source: The Operation of Consciousness (AGI-25, Reykjavik)

mentions.quote: So functionalism to me is simply the recognition of how we can construct objects.
mentions.source: Machine Learning Street Talk – Why Leibniz Couldn't Find the Mind Inside the Mill (Joscha Bach)

facets.label: Computationalism, weak and strong
facets.bach_take: This is Bach's core thesis across the series: a new monism in which information and computation are primary. Later he sharpens it: no implementable language can do more than a finite automaton.

mentions.quote: but rather computationalism, which means that information and computation are primary.
mentions.source: How to Build a Mind: Artificial Intelligence Reloaded (30C3)

mentions.quote: strong computationalism basically no implementable language can do more than a finite automaton
mentions.source: Synthetic Sentience (37C3)

facets.label: Stanisław Lem
facets.bach_take: Bach calls Lem an 'ingenious' author and 'cybernetic philosopher' and reads Golem XIV as an early picture of a large language model that outthinks scientists. He already cited Lem's Star Diaries in his thesis.

mentions.quote: basically the great author of Cybernetics has influenced me
mentions.source: Lex Fridman Podcast #101 – Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality

mentions.quote: the ingenious Polish science fiction author and cybernetic philosopher Stanislaw Lem
mentions.source: The age of AGE: Artificial General Experience (Joscha Bach, Substack; text written for Rana Gujral's book 'The AI Instinct')

mentions.quote: listed in the dissertation bibliography (Lem 1971, The Star Diaries).
mentions.source: Principles of Synthetic Intelligence: Building Blocks for an Architecture of Motivated Cognition (PhD dissertation draft, Universität Osnabrück)

mentions.quote: Bach says Lem (a friend of someone in Dörner's circle) became a philosophical science-fiction author to be free of the constraints of academia.
mentions.source: The Jim Rutt Show EP72 – Joscha Bach on Minds, Machines & Magic

mentions.quote: 'Lem's Golem computer is a Large Language Model, capable of running circles around the best human scientists'.
mentions.source: The age of AGE: Artificial General Experience (Joscha Bach, Substack; text written for Rana Gujral's book 'The AI Instinct')

mentions.quote: Solaris (1961) is in the CIMC library under science fiction.
mentions.source: cimc.ai library (reading list)

facets.label: Solaris
facets.bach_take: Bach's image for what Earth becomes if one agent colonises all its matter: a thinking planet. He also takes from Lem the idea that very different levels of intelligence may be unable to communicate.

mentions.quote: I am a thinking a thinking planet
mentions.source: Lex Fridman Podcast #101 – Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality

mentions.quote: a thinking system that is realizing what it is
mentions.source: Joscha Bach Λ Karl Friston: Ai, Death, Self, God, Consciousness (Theories of Everything)

mentions.quote: I've got a lot of useful ideas from reading thinkers like Stanislav Llem
mentions.source: Joscha Bach: "You Are Not Who You Think You Are!" (Dr Brian Keating, Into the Impossible)

facets.label: Summa Technologiae
facets.bach_take: Bach cites an argument in it against psi phenomena: if precognition were real, casinos and lotteries would not keep winning.

mentions.quote: It’s an argument that for instance has been made by Stanislaw Lem in I think Summa Technologiae
mentions.source: The Jim Rutt Show EP87 – Joscha Bach on Theories of Consciousness

facets.bach_take: In Q&A Bach says academia has become industrialised normal science, which makes new paradigms hard. He finds it striking that when the term was coined, Minsky and Chomsky next door were still founding whole fields.

mentions.quote: kuhn's invention of normal science also happened at the same time
mentions.source: Singularity.FM – Joscha Bach on AI, Cosmology, Existence and the Bible

mentions.quote: this idea of normal science was also a new paradigm
mentions.source: Cyber Animism (talk hosted by Michael Levin's center, Tufts)

facets.bach_take: Bach's example of what Roko's basilisk would need to be in order to work: a pre-committed, inevitable trigger.

mentions.quote: something like a doomsday machine, as in Dr. Strangelove
mentions.source: Lex Fridman Podcast #392 – Joscha Bach: Life, Intelligence, Consciousness, AI & the Future of Humans

facets.bach_take: Bach uses it as his measure of a good world model and says machine-learning models of the mind approximate it. He applies it to the simulation question: the best model is the shortest one that predicts our observations.

mentions.quote: And we can mathematically prove that we can not do better than Solomonoff induction.
mentions.source: Computational Meta-Psychology (32C3)

mentions.quote: I think that Ray Solomonoff had a good idea when he defined the limit of the quality of such a world model
mentions.source: Do we live in a simulation or in the base reality? (bach.ai blog)

mentions.quote: you have to find the shortest program among the best programs that predicts your current observation from past observations
mentions.source: Machine Dreams (33C3)

mentions.quote: Solomonoff induction where you are trying to understand intelligence as predicting future observations from past observations
mentions.source: Lex Fridman Podcast #392 – Joscha Bach: Life, Intelligence, Consciousness, AI & the Future of Humans

mentions.quote: 'Machine learning models of the mind can be understood as approximating Solomonoff induction (see Hutter 2005)'.
mentions.source: The Cortical Conductor Theory: Towards Addressing Consciousness in AI Models (BICA 2018)

mentions.quote: Bach lists 'Turing, Minsky, von Neumann, Solomonoff, many many others' as people who anticipated and helped bring about AI
mentions.source: The Spirit in the Machine | feat. Joscha Bach (AM I? podcast; YouTube also shows the alternate titles 'The Quest to Build Conscious AI' and 'Deepfaking the Human Mind')

facets.bach_take: Bach credits him as one of the first inventors of function approximation as used in deep learning.

mentions.quote: Paraphrase (garbled as 'Alex iako'): Alexey Ivakhnenko and others defined function approximation and learning in ways still used in deep learning.
mentions.source: Synthetic Sentience (37C3)

mentions.quote: Paraphrase (garbled as 'Alexander ieno'): deep learning has been invented multiple times, and one of the first was Ivakhnenko.
mentions.source: Cyber Animism (talk hosted by Michael Levin's center, Tufts)

facets.bach_take: Bach compares religious prophets to Paul 'vibing with the future' and foreseeing minds merging into one agent.

mentions.quote: Bach compares the Christian rapture prophecy to what Paul 'is doing in Dune', seeing what is likely to happen
mentions.source: Joscha Bach: "You Are Not Who You Think You Are!" (Dr Brian Keating, Into the Impossible)

facets.label: Lord of Light and Amber
facets.bach_take: A shared favourite of Bach and Steve Hsu. Bach relates shifting between Amber's worlds to changing feature dimensions in a lucid dream and suspects Zelazny discovered this through lucid dreaming.

mentions.quote: treating reality is a lucid dream in which you slowly, gradually move the feature dimensions
mentions.source: Manifold #76 (Steve Hsu) – Joscha Bach: Consciousness and AGI

mentions.quote: I'm not sure if creatures of light and darkness can be turned into a movie.
mentions.source: Manifold #76 (Steve Hsu) – Joscha Bach: Consciousness and AGI

facets.label: He Who Shapes
facets.bach_take: Bach cites it as an early picture of generative AI used as controllable immersive therapy, and of augmenting minds rather than replacing them.

mentions.quote: it's a short story in which he is describing how to use a generative AI for therapy purposes
mentions.source: Manifold #76 (Steve Hsu) – Joscha Bach: Consciousness and AGI

mentions.quote: He Who Shapes (1965) is listed under sci-fi.
mentions.source: cimc.ai library (reading list)

facets.label: Symbolic AI and expert systems
facets.bach_take: Bach says this approach turned out to be brittle with diminishing returns, mirrors Wittgenstein's failed project, and was overtaken by sub-symbolic learning; he expects meta-learning next.

mentions.quote: This turned out to be brittle, and difficult, and had diminishing returns.
mentions.source: How to Build a Mind: Artificial Intelligence Reloaded (30C3)

mentions.quote: And symbolic AI was mostly similar to Wittgenstein's program.
mentions.source: The Ghost in the Machine (35C3)

facets.label: Newell and Simon
facets.bach_take: Bach says that as an undergraduate he wanted to learn about Minsky, Newell and Simon, found nobody teaching them, and organised the lectures himself.

mentions.quote: I had to offer these lectures myself as an undergrad
mentions.source: Salon with Stephen Wolfram × Joscha Bach_What if we had bigger brains. (California Institute for Machine Consciousness)

facets.bach_take: Bach and Sorensen use it to show that people are easily fooled by surface behaviour, which is one reason they say behaviour tests cannot settle consciousness.

mentions.quote: among criticisms of the Turing Test is 'Joseph Weizenbaum's discovery that non-expert humans talking to computer programs can often be fooled by superficial appearances of intelligent behavior'.
mentions.source: The Machine Consciousness Hypothesis (Joscha Bach & Hikari Sorensen, CIMC essay)

facets.bach_take: Bach notes that many people once took this as the definition of AGI, and that we arguably have it now, which shows the goalposts need rethinking.

mentions.quote: a lot of people thought having a system that is like in Star Trek
mentions.source: Joscha Bach - Why Your Thoughts Aren't Yours. (Machine Learning Street Talk)

brautigan.title: All Watched Over by Machines of Loving Grace

facets.bach_take: The 38C3 title 'Self Models of Loving Grace' alludes to it, and Bach ends by hoping for a relationship of 'loving grace' with machines. He does not name the poem or the poet in the transcript.

mentions.quote: Bach hopes we can build a relationship of loving grace to the machines that watch over us.
mentions.source: Self Models of Loving Grace (38C3)

leary.title: Timothy Leary and the eight-circuit model

facets.bach_take: A cautionary example for Bach: psychedelics can make everything seem explained while a person loses touch with reality (overfitting). He also notes they sometimes help (e.g. cluster headaches) and can open the 'enlightenment' stage.

mentions.quote: he has written beautiful manifestos about the effect of LSD on people
mentions.source: Lex Fridman Podcast #212 – Joscha Bach: Nature of Reality, Dreams, and Consciousness

mentions.quote: 'Timothy Leary's eight circuits, which have been adapted by the great Robert Anton Wilson'.
mentions.source: Levels of Lucidity (Joscha Bach, Substack)

facets.bach_take: Bach's default physics. Since only computation can be constructed, any consistent description of the universe must be computational. He calls the result a 'causally closed lookup table' whose computer we cannot inspect.

mentions.quote: he actually believed that the physical universe is probably in some server farm in the parent universe
mentions.source: Manifold #76 (Steve Hsu) – Joscha Bach: Consciousness and AGI

mentions.quote: Paraphrase (garbled as 'Conrad Suzu ... Ed Fratkin and Stephen Wolfram'): digital physics, in the tradition of Konrad Zuse, Ed Fredkin and Stephen Wolfram, describes the universe as a cellular automaton.
mentions.source: Machine Dreams (33C3)

mentions.quote: Paraphrase (German): Konrad Zuse was the first to think the universe might be a computer, in 'Rechnender Raum'.
mentions.source: Machine Dreams (German-language lecture, Dresden / Datenspuren 2017)

facets.bach_take: Bach's standard picture of a universe: a simple rule in which stable, moving patterns ('particles') and eventually controllers can emerge. He also shows a continuous variant with cell-like blobs.

mentions.quote: the most famous automaton is Conway's Game of Life; it has gliders and spaceships, is Turing complete, and a continuous version with discs produces smoother moving patterns.
mentions.source: Machine Dreams (33C3)

facets.bach_take: Bach uses the line to ask whether AI could be fully intelligent without the coherence-creating process we call consciousness.

mentions.quote: it was quite possible that he had created intelligent beings with no souls
mentions.source: The Operation of Consciousness (AGI-25, Reykjavik)

facets.bach_take: In 2014 Bach argues it is neither necessary nor sufficient for consciousness (elephants and dogs fail for irrelevant reasons). In 2024 he playfully runs a version on Claude by feeding it screenshots of its own chat.

mentions.quote: it's actually not a test of consciousness, but it's a test of your ability to recognize that the mirror shows your body surface
mentions.source: From Computation to Consciousness (31C3)

mentions.quote: It’s interesting to see my own description being shown back to to me is part of the conversation
mentions.source: Self Models of Loving Grace (38C3)

facets.bach_take: Curt Jaimungal raised it; Bach said he never understood how it explains consciousness, because he saw no specification he could implement.

mentions.quote: I didn't quite understand how it was explaining consciousness.
mentions.source: Joscha Bach: Time, Simulation Hypothesis, Existence (Theories of Everything with Curt Jaimungal)

dreyfus.title: Dreyfus: What Computers Still Can't Do

facets.bach_take: Bach cites Dreyfus for the weakness of purely symbolic systems in real-world grounding, without giving up on computational models of mind.

mentions.quote: symbolic AI 'is also difficult to ground into real world interactions and to scale upon dynamic environments (see, for instance, Dreyfus 1992)'.
mentions.source: Principles of Synthetic Intelligence: Building Blocks for an Architecture of Motivated Cognition (PhD dissertation draft, Universität Osnabrück)

mentions.quote: reference [5] Dreyfus (1992).
mentions.source: Seven Principles of Synthetic Intelligence (Proc. 1st Conference on Artificial General Intelligence, Memphis, pp. 63-74)

facets.bach_take: Bach imagines AI merging with biological computation into a planetary agent, a 'Gaia' or 'hyper Gaia', and says humanity's actual role has been to burn fossil fuel rather than serve Gaia.

mentions.quote: some Gaia is being built over the entirety of all digital and biological computation
mentions.source: Lex Fridman Podcast #392 – Joscha Bach: Life, Intelligence, Consciousness, AI & the Future of Humans

mentions.quote: our purpose on earth is apparently not to serve Gaia
mentions.source: The Jim Rutt Show Currents 083 – Joscha Bach on Synthetic Intelligence

mentions.quote: we are not good stewards of Gaia
mentions.source: Joscha Bach and Connor Leahy [HQ VERSION] (Machine Learning Street Talk)

mentions.quote: maybe the smartest thing on the planet is Gaia
mentions.source: Joscha Bach: Consciousness, Artificial Intelligence, and the Threat of AI Apocalypse (Robinson Erhardt / Robinson's Podcast)

mentions.quote: Paraphrase (captions: 'go beyond Gaia alone and build hyperia'): we can teach the rocks to think, go beyond Gaia and build a next-level system that becomes coherent over the whole planet and might integrate us.
mentions.source: Synthetic Sentience (37C3)

facets.bach_take: Bach read it as a child and says he went through then what Greta Thunberg's generation feels now. AI interests him partly because it reopens a future he had assumed was closing.

mentions.quote: I read the Club of Rome report on the limits to growth
mentions.source: This is the dawn of machine consciousness | Joscha Bach FULL INTERVIEW (Institute of Art and Ideas)

nagel.title: Nagel: What Is It Like to Be a Bat?
