facets.bach_take: Bach uses the phrase 'what it's like' as his definition of phenomenology, parodies the argument ('what is it like to be a bird? You'll never know'), and lists Nagel among philosophers who find machine consciousness preposterous.

mentions.quote: they will tell you, what is it like to be a bird? You'll never know.
mentions.source: Machine Dreams (33C3)

mentions.quote: some philosophers think machine consciousness is a preposterous idea, 'like Anil Seth and Thomas Nagel and so on and Ned Block'.
mentions.source: The Operation of Consciousness (AGI-25, Reykjavik)

mentions.quote: the issue 'has been described by many others, such as Thomas Nagel in his famous essay “What Is It Like to Be a Bat?”'.
mentions.source: The Machine Consciousness Hypothesis (Joscha Bach & Hikari Sorensen, CIMC essay)

facets.bach_take: Bach cites it for the warning against 'methodologism': letting the tools you already have decide which questions you ask. This became his second principle, 'Avoid methodologism'.

mentions.quote: Avoid methodologism
mentions.source: Seven Principles of Synthetic Intelligence (Proc. 1st Conference on Artificial General Intelligence, Memphis, pp. 63-74)

mentions.quote: one should not fall victim to 'methodologism', ignoring what lies outside the methodology already at hand (Feyerabend 1975).
mentions.source: Principles of Synthetic Intelligence: Building Blocks for an Architecture of Motivated Cognition (PhD dissertation draft, Universität Osnabrück)

facets.bach_take: Bach's explanation for norms, honour and the sense of the sacred: evolution needs ways to keep groups full of 'angels', and in humans that is an internalised reputation system.

mentions.quote: we are subject to multilevel selection inside of our organism.
mentions.source: Machine Dreams (33C3)

mentions.quote: we basically are multi-level selection species.
mentions.source: The Ghost in the Machine (35C3)

facets.bach_take: Bach presents it as the position behind symbolic architectures and sets it against connectionist replies, as part of asking what kind of representation a mind needs.

mentions.quote: our language of thought our mental lease is in some sense the programming language of our own mind
mentions.source: Synthetic Sentience (37C3)

mentions.quote: 'The Language Of Thought Hypothesis (LOTH) is usually attributed to Jerry Fodor (1975)', and it tries to explain how a material thing can have semantic properties.
mentions.source: Principles of Synthetic Intelligence: Building Blocks for an Architecture of Motivated Cognition (PhD dissertation draft, Universität Osnabrück)

mentions.quote: reference [14] Fodor (1975).
mentions.source: Seven Principles of Synthetic Intelligence (Proc. 1st Conference on Artificial General Intelligence, Memphis, pp. 63-74)

facets.bach_take: The CIMC essay says Grossberg came up with a model similar to the attention-control account; his 2021 book is in the CIMC library.

mentions.quote: The neuroscientist Grossberg has come up with the cognitive architecture that he calls the adaptive resonance theory.
mentions.source: Lex Fridman Podcast #392 – Joscha Bach: Life, Intelligence, Consciousness, AI & the Future of Humans

mentions.quote: Adaptive resonance theory that explains it as some kind of resonance between um um neural activation states.
mentions.source: The Operation of Consciousness (AGI-25, Reykjavik)

mentions.quote: 'The neuroscientist Stephen Grossberg came up with a similar model in the context of' his Adaptive Resonance Theory.
mentions.source: The Machine Consciousness Hypothesis (Joscha Bach & Hikari Sorensen, CIMC essay)

mentions.quote: Conscious Mind, Resonant Brain (2021) is in the CIMC library.
mentions.source: cimc.ai library (reading list)

facets.bach_take: Bach describes religions and ideologies as mind viruses with immune systems, and civilisation as partly the result of selecting people susceptible to the same ones.

mentions.quote: pushed back against the religious mind virus that had controlled the world until then
mentions.source: Singularity.FM – Joscha Bach: We need to understand the nature of AI to understand who we are

mentions.quote: people in it, they’re very susceptible to this same mind viruses
mentions.source: The Jim Rutt Show EP72 – Joscha Bach on Minds, Machines & Magic

mentions.quote: Dawkins says no, it's actually about certain molecules, the genes that are just using the organism as a mechanism to replicate.
mentions.source: AGI-24 keynote on cyber animism (Seattle; Machine Learning Street Talk recording)

mentions.quote: Darwin says evolution is the competition between species
mentions.source: Joscha Bach - Why Your Thoughts Aren't Yours. (Machine Learning Street Talk)

mentions.quote: Paraphrase (captions: 'for Darin ... then dokins comes along'): for Darwin evolution is competition between organisms; Dawkins says what matters are the genes.
mentions.source: Cyber Animism (talk hosted by Michael Levin's center, Tufts)

facets.bach_take: Bach likes the picture but says the book has the wrong name: it is about the origin of the personal self and the breakdown of the polytheist mind, not about consciousness. He uses it to define gods as selves that span several minds.

mentions.quote: Julian James wrote the famous book the origin of Consciousness and the breakdown of the bamal mind this book has the wrong name
mentions.source: Synthetic Sentience (37C3)

facets.bach_take: Bach's Request Confirmation Networks are built to run script-like hierarchical plans in a neural style, joining top-down requests with bottom-up confirmation.

mentions.quote: ReCoNs are spreading activation networks with units that contain an activation and a state
mentions.source: Request confirmation networks for neuro-symbolic script execution (Bach & Herger, CoCo workshop at NIPS 2015)

mentions.quote: listed in the dissertation bibliography (Schank & Abelson 1977).
mentions.source: Principles of Synthetic Intelligence: Building Blocks for an Architecture of Motivated Cognition (PhD dissertation draft, Universität Osnabrück)

facets.bach_take: A joke about how fast the mind boots: a child has been awake about 80 megaseconds by age two and a half, enough to understand Star Wars, and everything after that is cosmetics.

mentions.quote: By this age you understand Star Wars. And I think that everything after understanding Star Wars is cosmetics.
mentions.source: Computational Meta-Psychology (32C3)

facets.bach_take: Bach uses a Sloman line as the motto for his chapter on cognitive architectures and compares Sloman's Cognition and Affect work with the Psi theory, calling it inspiring but not very detailed.

mentions.quote: “Every intelligent ghost must contain a machine.” Aaron Sloman (2002)
mentions.source: Principles of Synthetic Intelligence: Building Blocks for an Architecture of Motivated Cognition (PhD dissertation draft, Universität Osnabrück)

mentions.quote: and then Aaron Sloman and Maggie Boden which are already far less known
mentions.source: The Spirit in the Machine | feat. Joscha Bach (AM I? podcast; YouTube also shows the alternate titles 'The Quest to Build Conscious AI' and 'Deepfaking the Human Mind')

mentions.quote: the preface mentions 'Aaron Sloman's inspiring but not very detailed Cognition and Affect architecture'.
mentions.source: Principles of Synthetic Intelligence: Building Blocks for an Architecture of Motivated Cognition (PhD dissertation draft, Universität Osnabrück)

facets.bach_take: Both books are in the CIMC library, and the whitepaper names Hofstadter with Dennett and Graziano. Bach's thesis cites Hofstadter 1995.

mentions.quote: I think that our consciousness is not strange as a loop.
mentions.source: Joscha Bach: Time, Simulation Hypothesis, Existence (Theories of Everything with Curt Jaimungal)

mentions.quote: listed in the dissertation bibliography (Hofstadter 1995).
mentions.source: Principles of Synthetic Intelligence: Building Blocks for an Architecture of Motivated Cognition (PhD dissertation draft, Universität Osnabrück)

mentions.quote: Possible garbled reference: 'an implement of loop theory, which is a recasting of Gödel’s proof'. Hofstadter is not named.
mentions.source: The Jim Rutt Show EP87 – Joscha Bach on Theories of Consciousness

mentions.quote: I Am a Strange Loop (2007) and The Mind's I (1981) are listed under modern texts.
mentions.source: cimc.ai library (reading list)

facets.bach_take: Bach uses it as an experiment anyone can run to see how low the fidelity of the brain's world model really is.

mentions.quote: put yourself into a lucid dream and look at the fidelity of what your brain is able to generate
mentions.source: Donald Hoffman Λ Joscha Bach: Consciousness, Gödel, Reality (Theories of Everything)

facets.label: The Thatcher illusion
facets.bach_take: Shown (without naming it) as evidence that we process facial features independently and then assemble them into a face schema.

mentions.quote: The thing that was odd about it in the first place was that the eyes and the mouth have been turned around
mentions.source: From Computation to Consciousness (31C3)

facets.label: The dress
facets.bach_take: Bach's opening joke in 2015 and his example that minds cannot know objective truths, only generate interpretations.

mentions.quote: What color is the dress
mentions.source: Computational Meta-Psychology (32C3)

facets.bach_take: Bach lists Searle among the standard objections to AI in 2008. The CIMC essay places the Chinese Room next to Leibniz's mill as an illustration of the gap that a functional account has to close, and does not accept Searle's conclusion.

mentions.quote: John Searle said— you know, Searle is the one with the Chinese room. We’re not going to go into that
mentions.source: How to Build a Mind: Artificial Intelligence Reloaded (30C3)

mentions.quote: So it’s intrinsic powers of biological neurons.
mentions.source: How to Build a Mind: Artificial Intelligence Reloaded (30C3)

mentions.quote: so you have your Chinese room or your unique position in about free will and you're going to defend this hill
mentions.source: Singularity.FM – Joscha Bach: We need to understand the nature of AI to understand who we are

mentions.quote: Searle's Chinese room argument that I think is a reformulation of Leibniz intuition pump
mentions.source: Joscha Bach: Time, Simulation Hypothesis, Existence (Theories of Everything with Curt Jaimungal)

mentions.quote: it's a very strong intuition that also drives the Chinese room
mentions.source: Machine Learning Street Talk #82 – Dr. Joscha Bach: Digital Physics, DL and Consciousness [UNPLUGGED]

mentions.quote: The issue with Searle is that there is very little for me to engage. There is a claim but no argument.
mentions.source: Why Consciousness Might Not Be Hard At All (Joscha Bach) (Machine Learning Street Talk)

mentions.quote: The issue with Searle is that there is very little for me to engage. There is a claim but no argument.
mentions.source: Machine Learning Street Talk – Why Leibniz Couldn't Find the Mind Inside the Mill (Joscha Bach)

mentions.quote: index entry 'Chinese Room argument'; bibliography lists Searle 1980, 1984, 1992.
mentions.source: Principles of Synthetic Intelligence: Building Blocks for an Architecture of Motivated Cognition (PhD dissertation draft, Universität Osnabrück)

mentions.quote: references [4] Searle (1992) The Rediscovery of the Mind and [9] Searle (1980) Minds, brains, and programs.
mentions.source: Seven Principles of Synthetic Intelligence (Proc. 1st Conference on Artificial General Intelligence, Memphis, pp. 63-74)

mentions.quote: 'Centuries later, John Searle's Chinese Room illustrates a similar gap in his perspective on computational systems', replacing Leibniz' machine with a computer.
mentions.source: The Machine Consciousness Hypothesis (Joscha Bach & Hikari Sorensen, CIMC essay)

facets.bach_take: An analogy for understanding: an observer inside the fractal sees only local regularities and can never guess the generating formula from within without a lucky leap.

mentions.quote: But imagine you live inside of this fractal and you don't have access to where you are in the fractal
mentions.source: Lex Fridman Podcast #101 – Joscha Bach: Artificial Consciousness and the Nature of Reality

mentions.quote: I think that pi is being constructed
mentions.source: Joscha Bach: Time, Simulation Hypothesis, Existence (Theories of Everything with Curt Jaimungal)

mentions.quote: imagine living inside the Mandelbrot fractal; you can predict shapes locally, but finding the formula requires stepping outside.
mentions.source: The Ghost in the Machine (35C3)

binding.title: The binding problem and neural synchrony

facets.label: The binding problem
facets.bach_take: Bach's 2019 paper turns the question around: consciousness is tied to the 'perceptual binding state', the moment-to-moment unified model that attention builds.

mentions.quote: 'In neuroscience, a similar approach is found in feature integration theory (Treisman and Gelade 1980). Another way of achieving binding is called synchronization theory (Milner 1974, von der Malsburg 1981)'.
mentions.source: Phenomenal Experience and the Perceptual Binding State (AAAI Spring Symposium workshop TOCAIS 2019, CEUR Vol-2287)

mentions.quote: a nonlocal version of synchronization theory 'is advanced by Crick and Koch (1990)'.
mentions.source: Phenomenal Experience and the Perceptual Binding State (AAAI Spring Symposium workshop TOCAIS 2019, CEUR Vol-2287)

mentions.quote: Pearce traces the binding problem to William James and argues AIs on digital computers 'at most ... are zombies'; Bach says he disagrees
mentions.source: The Panel Where Everyone Disagrees About Saving the World - Joscha Bach, David Pearce, Andrew Critch (California Institute for Machine Consciousness)

facets.label: Wolf Singer and 40 Hz synchrony
facets.bach_take: Bach says he did not understand it as an explanation: oscillations may be necessary for neurons to coordinate, but the theory does not say why they would be sufficient.

mentions.quote: who suggested that consciousness is a 40 hertz oscillation in the brain.
mentions.source: From Computation to Consciousness (31C3)

mentions.quote: it didn’t make functional sense
mentions.source: The Jim Rutt Show EP87 – Joscha Bach on Theories of Consciousness

facets.label: Christoph von der Malsburg
